Frank Sturgis (1924 – 1993) was one of the five Watergate burglars whose capture led to the end of the Presidency of Richard Nixon. He served in several branches of the United States military and in the Cuban Revolution of 1958, and worked as a mercenary and undercover operative.

In 1942, at age 17, he joined the United States Marine Corps and served in the Pacific during WW2. In 1946 he joined the Norfolk police department and discovered a corrupt payoff system which he was told to overlook and so he resigned and for the next 18 months managed the Havana-Madrid tavern in Norfolk that catered Cuban merchant seamen.

In 1947, Sturgis joined the United States Naval Reserve and learned to fly while still working at the tavern. In 1948 he joined the United States Army and was sent to West Berlin where he worked as a Marine Raider gathering intelligence behind enemy lines.

Sturgis moved to Miami in 1957, where he was introduced to former Cuban president Carlos Prio, and joined him in opposing dictator Batista and plotting their return to power. Sturgis then met up with Castro and his 400 rebels in the Sierra Maestra mountains and, after smuggling in boatloads of CIA weapons, trained Che Guevera and his troops in guerrilla warfare.

As seen in this photo, when Castro seized power, Fiorini was part of a firing squad on San Juan Hill on January 11, 1959, that executed 71 of their opponents into an awaiting 40-foot ditch that had been opened with a bulldozer. Castro then appointed Sturgis gambling czar and director of security and intelligence for the air force, in addition to his position as a captain in the 26th of July Movement. Sturgis defected the following month and joined the anti-Castro exile opposition.

In 1963, Sturgis was the subject of allegations regarding the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. Specifically, it has been alleged that he was one of the three tramps photographed by several Dallas newspapers under police escort near the Texas School Book Depository shortly after the assassination of JFK.

On June 17, 1972, Sturgis and four others were arrested while installing electronic listening devices in the national Democratic Party campaign offices located at the Watergate office complex in Washington, a discovery that led to the resignation of President Nixon. He served 10 months in prison. At the same time he was convicted of running an international car theft ring for which he served 14 months.

After release, Sturgis returned to Miami and continued with his anti-Castro activities. He also traveled to Angola and Honduras to train US-backed rebels. While in Africa he met with persons such as Venezuelan terrorist Carlos the Jackal and Yassir Arafat.
